title: 🤖 Wayland: Use unaccelerated relative motion when the mouse is captured
body:
> [!INFO] *AI disclosure*: This contribution was authored by an autonomous AI agent (Claude Code), on behalf of a user to fix (unlinked by bugsquad) #123793, which that user reported. The agent read the Wayland backend, wrote the patch, built a `template_release` binary and ran the measurement below; the user asked for the PR and approved submitting it.

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

With `MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED` on the Wayland backend, `InputEventMouseMotion.relative` / `screen_relative` carry the compositor's **accelerated** delta (`dx`/`dy` from `zwp_relative_pointer_v1.relative_motion`), so camera look speed depends on how fast the mouse is moved and on the desktop's pointer-acceleration profile. The X11 backend (XInput2 raw events) and the Windows backend (raw input) both report unaccelerated motion while the mouse is captured, so the same game feels different on Wayland.

## Additional information

The `relative_motion` event already delivers `dx_unaccel`/`dy_unaccel`, which `_wp_relative_pointer_on_relative_motion` currently ignores. This PR stores them next to the accelerated pair, and the pointer frame uses them for `relative` **only while the pointer is locked** (`PointerConstraint::LOCKED`, i.e. `MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED`). That matches the other two backends, which also use raw motion only in captured mode. Visible, confined and hidden modes are unchanged, and so are `position` and `velocity`.

**Measured.** A uinput virtual mouse sent bursts of a fixed 256 device counts at 125 Hz, at six per-event sizes, first ascending and then descending. A minimal project captured the mouse and logged every `screen_relative.x`. The value below is the gain, `sum(screen_relative.x) / 256`, averaged over the ascending and descending passes. The same exported pack ran on the official 4.7.2-stable `linux_release` template and on a `template_release` built from 4.7.2-stable with this patch (`production=yes`). The patch applies unchanged to `master`. KDE Plasma / KWin 6.7.5, libinput pointer profile **Adaptive** (the KDE default), NVIDIA 580, two runs per arm with identical results:

| counts per event | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4.7.2-stable, Wayland | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.10 | 1.63 | 1.93 | 1.94 |
| **This PR, Wayland** | **1.00** | **1.00** | **1.00** | **1.00** | **1.00** | **1.00** |
| 4.7.2-stable, X11 (XWayland), for reference | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 |

**Not tested:** compositors other than KWin (GNOME/Mutter, wlroots-based), real hardware other than the virtual device, and a build of `master` itself (tested on the 4.7.2-stable backport of the identical diff). The protocol notes that the unaccelerated delta "does not represent 'raw' events" and may equal the accelerated one on some devices. For a Flat profile that means no change, which is the expected result.
